topIssues.title: kona/protocol: brotli decoder (brotli-decompressor) is more lenient than op-node (andybalholm) — accepts malformed channels op-node rejects
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
## Summary

Differential testing of the two brotli decoders used in OP Stack derivation — `brotli-decompressor` 5.0.1 (kona, [`decompress_brotli`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/44e40ba521c9ec2ad02f3ed7db3e79055afa9877/rust/kona/crates/protocol/protocol/src/brotli.rs#L19-L90)) vs `andybalholm/brotli` v1.1.0 (op-node, [`BatchReader`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/44e40ba521c9ec2ad02f3ed7db3e79055afa9877/op-node/rollup/derive/channel.go#L174-L219)) — shows the two disagree on brotli **validity**. The consensus-relevant direction: **kona's decoder accepts malformed channels that op-node rejects.** kona would then RLP-decode batches op-node discards. If any such batch is valid, kona advances the safe chain where op-node does not → consensus split. This is the mirror image of #20666 (which worried about the opposite direction — that one turns out to be structurally impossible for the current eager decoder).

This is the *residual* decoder gap behind [protocol-team#84 (strict channel decompression)](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/84): strict semantics remove the unbounded partial-output surface but leave this validity-boundary disagreement, which needs decoder conformance work.

## Evidence

Over 70,526 adversarial streams (corruptions + truncations + fuzz), classifying each by whether the decoder reaches a *clean* end-of-stream:

| | count |
|---|---|
| both decoders accept | 58,695 |
| …of which **byte-length mismatch** | **0** |
| both reject | 5,941 |
| **kona accepts, op-node rejects** (kona too lenient) | **242** |
| kona rejects, op-node accepts (op-node too lenient) | 5,648 |

Key facts:
- **Accepted streams never diverge** (0 length mismatches) — valid brotli is deterministic. All divergence is at the accept/reject boundary.
- The 242 kona-too-lenient cases collapse to two root causes: `BLOCK_LENGTH_1/2` (98) and `excessive input` (144).

## Root cause 1 — `BLOCK_LENGTH` (confirmed, fix in hand)

`brotli-decompressor`'s `BROTLI_STATE_METABLOCK_DONE` handler is **missing the `meta_block_remaining_len < 0` check** that andybalholm ([decode.go#L2464-L2468](https://github.com/andybalholm/brotli/blob/v1.1.0/decode.go#L2464-L2468)) and the C reference enforce. When a metablock's insert-copy commands overshoot the declared MLEN, `meta_block_remaining_len` goes negative; the command loop breaks to `METABLOCK_DONE`, which runs cleanup and proceeds to `SUCCESS` without validating. andybalholm rejects with `BLOCK_LENGTH_2`.

Confirmed by red/green in an isolated copy of the crate: unpatched accepts **98/98** of the malformed streams; with a 5-line check added it accepts **0/98** (matching andybalholm), and all valid streams still decode:

```diff
         BrotliRunningState::BROTLI_STATE_METABLOCK_DONE => {
+          if (s.meta_block_remaining_len < 0) {
+            result = BrotliDecoderErrorCode::BROTLI_DECODER_ERROR_FORMAT_BLOCK_LENGTH_2;
+            break;
+          }
           s.BrotliStateCleanupAfterMetablock();
```

This is the **same class** as the PADDING_2 fix ([dropbox/rust-brotli-decompressor#44](https://github.com/dropbox/rust-brotli-decompressor/pull/44)) — a missing end-of-metablock validation in the very same state handler. It needs an **upstream fix in `brotli-decompressor`**, then a version bump here (like #21505 did for PADDING_2).

## Root cause 2 — `excessive input` (trailing bytes)

andybalholm rejects a stream with bytes remaining after the final metablock (`excessive input`); `brotli-decompressor` stops at the ISLAST metablock and returns success, ignoring the trailing bytes. **Fixable at the kona wrapper** by requiring the input reader to be fully consumed — the `decompress_brotli_strict` "reader fully consumed" check floated in #20666 (the one sound idea there). Under strict semantics this is the natural rule: a channel with trailing garbage is invalid.

## Reverse direction (for completeness)

The 5,648 "op-node accepts, kona rejects" cases are **89% truncations**: andybalholm treats a truncated stream as clean (returns partial output, nil error), while `brotli-decompressor` correctly rejects it (RFC 7932: a truncated stream is invalid). Here **andybalholm** is the lenient/non-conformant side. This direction also causes divergence (op-node ahead) and needs an op-node-side decision, since op-node is the incumbent.

## Relationship to strict decompression (protocol-team#84)

Strict semantics are the right foundation and should land regardless — they guarantee accepted channels produce identical output and delete the entire best-effort partial-output surface. But strict is **necessary, not sufficient**: it reduces the problem from "identical partial bytes on every malformed stream" (implementation-defined, ~impossible) to "agree on validity" (a spec-defined boolean) — and the decoders still disagree on that boolean. Closing it is the bounded conformance work below.

## Proposed work

- [ ] Upstream `brotli-decompressor`: add the `BLOCK_LENGTH_2` check to `METABLOCK_DONE` (patch above; sibling to #44) — PR up at dropbox/rust-brotli-decompressor#47; then bump the pin here once it releases.
- [ ] kona wrapper: require the input reader fully consumed → rejects `excessive input` — **#84-gated; do NOT land standalone.** Under today's best-effort rule op-node already keeps the valid-portion batches from an `excessive input` channel (its "excessive input" error routes through the same `NextChannel` + keep-partial path as `io.EOF`), and kona agrees (it ignores the trailing bytes and decodes the same batches). Adding this check now would make kona drop those batches (0 for the whole channel, via `decompress_brotli(...)?`) → a *new* kona-too-strict divergence. It reaches parity only once #84 makes op-node reject the whole channel too. (Same #84-gating applies to every "make the decoder stricter" step here, incl. the dropbox#47 `BLOCK_LENGTH` bump: today both clients keep partial batches and agree; tightening one side alone breaks that.)
- [x] op-node/andybalholm truncation direction — bumped op-node to andybalholm v1.2.2 (#21799, **merged**). The decoder now rejects truncated streams per RFC 7932 §9.3, matching the C reference and kona. The bump is behaviorally inert on its own (verified byte-identical batch output v1.1.0 vs v1.2.2); it provides the `io.ErrUnexpectedEOF` signal that the strict-decompression rule handling (below) acts on.
- [ ] Land protocol-team#84 (strict decompression) as the foundational rule change — includes the op-node rule handling that acts on the new `ErrUnexpectedEOF` signal to reject truncated channels, plus kona going strict.
- [ ] Gate a Go↔Rust differential *validity* fuzzer in CI (now feasible — it compares a boolean, not byte sequences).

## Methodology

Differential harness: kona's `brotli-decompressor` decode status vs `andybalholm/brotli` `io.ReadAll` over a shared corpus (corruptions of valid streams, truncations, random fuzz). Root cause confirmed by red/green against an isolated copy of `brotli-decompressor` 5.0.1. Harnesses and the 98 `BLOCK_LENGTH` reproducers are available on request.

## References

- #20666 — proposed the opposite-direction fix (refuted; the current eager decoder can't lag op-node)
- #19333 / #20598 / #20004 — original brotli divergence investigation and Bug 1/Bug 2 fixes
- #21505 — the PADDING_2 bump (brotli-decompressor 5.0.1)
- [dropbox/rust-brotli-decompressor#44](https://github.com/dropbox/rust-brotli-decompressor/pull/44) — PADDING_2 fix (same bug class)
- [protocol-team#84](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/84) — strict channel decompression

topIssues.title: kona/protocol: switch decompress_brotli to BrotliDecompressCustomIoCustomDict for incremental-flush parity with op-node
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
## Context

Follow-up from #19333 / #20598.

#20598 fixed a wrapper-level bug where `kona::decompress_brotli` under-produced output bytes on the truncation path (`NeedsMoreInput` raised with both `available_in` and `available_out` at 0). With that fix and the brotli crate's PADDING_2 fall-through patched upstream, the OP-Stack differential sweep on a 20-batch fixture (`investigate/brotli-divergence/driver.py` on branch `seb/investigate/kona-brotli-divergence`) converges to **0 BatchReader-level divergences** between kona and op-node.

But there's a residual **byte-level** divergence on the `ResultFailure with bytes already produced` path that hasn't been observed to affect batch counts in our existing fixtures, but is reachable in principle.

## The remaining divergence

Empirically (using `investigate/brotli-lib-diff/` on the same branch), on the *patched* Rust `brotli` crate, the high-level `BrotliDecompress` and the equivalent Go libraries differ on mid-stream `ResultFailure`:

Test input: 4 KB ascending-bytes plaintext, 259 B compressed by cbrotli, single-byte XOR at offset 19.

|   | status | partial bytes returned |
|---|---|---|
| `brotli::BrotliDecompress` (patched) | err | **0** |
| `andybalholm/brotli` via `io.ReadAll` | err | **512** |
| `google/brotli/go/cbrotli` via `io.ReadAll` | err | **512** |

Same difference shows up in our wrapper (`decompress_brotli`) vs op-node's `BatchReader`:

|   | DECOMPRESS_RESULT | bytes | BATCH_COUNT |
|---|---|---|---|
| kona (`decompress_brotli`) | err | 0 | 0 |
| op-node (`BatchReader`) | err | 512 | 0 |

They agree at the batch level *here* because the 512 partial bytes happen not to RLP-decode into a valid `BatchData`. But there is a class of adversarial inputs — a multi-batch channel where corruption is placed past the first batch boundary — where op-node's incremental flush would decode batch 1 successfully and then fail on batch 2, while kona would emit zero bytes and decode zero batches. That's a real, latent consensus-relevant divergence in op-node's favor.

## Root cause

`brotli::BrotliDecompressStream` only flushes its internal ringbuffer to the caller's output buffer at certain points (most notably `WriteRingBuffer` invocations). When the caller-supplied output buffer is large enough to hold the entire stream, brotli accumulates many decoded bytes in the ringbuffer before flushing. If `ResultFailure` is signaled before that flush happens, the bytes are lost from the caller's perspective even though they are valid decoded output up to the point of corruption.

Go's `brotli.NewReader` and `cbrotli.NewReader` paper over this by repeatedly invoking the C decoder with the small per-call read buffer the user supplies. Each `Read()` triggers a flush from the ringbuffer into the user's buffer, so the partial bytes for earlier metablocks are returned to the caller (via `io.ReadAll`) before a later metablock errors.

kona's hand-rolled wrapper in `rust/kona/crates/protocol/protocol/src/brotli.rs` does not replicate that pattern. It grows a single output buffer and re-enters `BrotliDecompressStream` rather than draining the ringbuffer between calls, so it tracks the underlying decoder's flush granularity rather than imposing its own.

## Proposed fix

Replace the hand-rolled `BrotliDecompressStream` loop in `kona::decompress_brotli` with `brotli::BrotliDecompressCustomIoCustomDict`. The crate exposes this no_std-friendly equivalent of the high-level Reader-based decompression:

- `CustomRead` / `CustomWrite` traits in `brotli::CustomRead` / `brotli::CustomWrite` are *not* `std`-gated (only the high-level `brotli::Decompressor` / `brotli::BrotliDecompress` are).
- `BrotliDecompressCustomIoCustomDict(reader, writer, in_buf, out_buf, ...)` runs the same incremental-flush loop as `BrotliDecompress` but on `CustomRead`/`CustomWrite`. It calls `BrotliDecompressStream` with a small fixed-size output buffer and writes each batch of produced bytes to the `CustomWrite` before continuing — exactly the pattern Go's reader uses.

Concretely:

1. Implement `CustomRead` for `&[u8]` (a few lines — track a cursor).
2. Implement `CustomWrite` for `Vec<u8>` with the size cap baked in: appends bytes, returns an error once `MAX_RLP_BYTES_PER_CHANNEL` is reached so the loop terminates per spec.
3. Replace the body of `decompress_brotli` with one call to `BrotliDecompressCustomIoCustomDict`. The existing `decompress_brotli_strict` variant becomes a thin wrapper that additionally checks the reader has been fully consumed.

This deletes the buffer-growth dance, the `NeedsMoreInput`-with-full-buffer workaround (#20598), and the implicit \"return what we have on `ResultFailure`\" behavior — and inherits Go-equivalent flush granularity for free, while preserving no_std compatibility.

## Validation

- Re-run the differential sweep (`investigate/brotli-divergence/driver.py`) at `N_BATCHES=20` and a few additional fixtures (multi-batch, multi-metablock, mid-stream corruption) and confirm 0 divergences at both the byte and batch level.
- Construct an adversarial multi-batch fixture where corruption is placed past the first batch boundary and confirm kona and op-node now agree on the batch count (op-node currently decodes batch 1; kona currently produces 0 batches).
- All existing `kona-protocol` tests continue to pass.

## Risks / considerations

- The change is wider than #20598 — it replaces the entire decompression loop rather than fixing a single match arm. Should land independently and get its own focused review.
- The `MAX_RLP_BYTES_PER_CHANNEL` size-cap-as-truncation semantics need to be preserved precisely (currently: cap exceeded → return truncated output, not an error). The `CustomWrite` impl needs to handle this carefully.
- Coordination point: the upstream `brotli-decompressor` PADDING_2 fix at the (independent) Rust crate level is necessary for this work to fully eliminate the kona/op-node divergence. Tracking upstream at dropbox/rust-brotli-decompressor#44.

## References

- #19333 — original divergence report (split into Bug 1 and Bug 2; this issue covers the residual byte-level part of Bug 1)
- #20598 — wrapper-bug fix that eliminates the truncation-side divergence
- #20004 — Bug 2 fix (Fjord gating via L1 origin)
- Investigation branch: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/tree/seb/investigate/kona-brotli-divergence/investigate
- Upstream brotli-decompressor PADDING_2 fix: dropbox/rust-brotli-decompressor#44

topPRs.title: chore: bump reth to include #26398 fix (validate_block_post_execution_with_hashed_state)
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Josh Klopfenstein** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0A3E04GDMX/p1784054235311919?thread_ts=1784054235.311919&cid=C0A3E04GDMX)_

Refs #21524

## Before

The Rust workspaces pinned `paradigmxyz/reth` to the **`v2.3.0`** release tag. reth `v2.4.0` shipped an incidental change to `validate_block_post_execution_with_hashed_state` that broke the OP Stack, so we could not simply move to the `v2.4.0` tag.

## After

The reth pin is moved to **`rev = "f2eecc65482af4085e43eedb27a32024bf177a0d"`** — the merge commit of paradigmxyz/reth#26398 (Sebastian Stammler's fix), which landed on `main` *after* the `v2.4.0` tag. This restores the `validate_block_post_execution_with_hashed_state` signature the OP Stack needs while picking up the rest of the 2.4.0 line. Because the fix is post-tag, we pin the commit (`rev`) rather than a tag, per `rust/UPDATING-RETH.md`.

Note this is a **two-release catch-up** (`v2.3.0` → post-`v2.4.0`), not a one-commit nudge — see "Remaining work" below.

## How

- Bump the reth git ref from `tag = "v2.3.0"` to `rev = "f2eecc65…"` across all **four** manifests the guide enumerates: `rust/Cargo.toml`, `rust/op-rbuilder/Cargo.toml`, `rust/rollup-boost/crates/rollup-boost/Cargo.toml`, `rust/rollup-boost/crates/flashblocks-rpc/Cargo.toml` (122 pin lines total).
- Sync the shared crates.io dependency versions to reth's pins at the new rev (read from reth's `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` at `f2eecc65…`):
  - `revm` family `40.x` → **`41.0.0`** (upstream unified all `revm-*` subcrates to `41.0.0`), `revm-inspectors` `0.40.1` → `0.41.0`; in `op-rbuilder`, `revm-context`/`revm-context-interface`/`revm-inspector` → `41.0.0`.
  - published reth-core crates (`reth-codecs`, `reth-codecs-derive`, `reth-primitives-traits`, `reth-rpc-traits`, `reth-zstd-compressors`) `0.4.1` → **`0.5.0`**.
  - alloy core (`alloy-consensus` … `alloy-transport*`) `2.0.x` → **`2.1.1`**, `alloy-evm` `0.36.0` → `0.37.0`, `alloy-eip7928` `0.4.0` → `0.4.5`, `alloy-rlp` `0.3.13` → `0.3.16`, `alloy-primitives`/`alloy-sol-types` bumped to `1.6.0` where they lagged.
  - OP-internal path crates (`op-revm`, `op-alloy*`, `alloy-op-evm`, `alloy-op-hardforks`) left untouched, per the guide.
- Update the replicated `SlotPreimages` MDBX-layout rev reference in `rust/op-reth/crates/cli/src/commands/slot_preimages_seed.rs`. I diffed the upstream `slot_preimages.rs` between `9384bc53…` (v2.3.0) and `f2eecc65…`: the byte-layout and insert/read logic are **identical** — only visibility (`pub`) and docs changed — so the replica stays byte-compatible and only the rev comment moved. (The upstream type becoming `pub` is what unblocks removing the replica in #21523.)

## Verification

⚠️ **Not built/resolved in this environment.** `cargo update` / `cargo check` against the new rev cannot run here: outbound git access to `github.com/paradigmxyz/reth` is blocked by egress policy (HTTP 403 through the agent proxy). Consequently:

- **Lockfiles are NOT regenerated** — the three `Cargo.lock` files still record the `v2.3.0` git source. They must be refreshed in an environment with reth access (`cargo update reth-chainspec` in `.`, `op-rbuilder/`, and `rollup-boost/`).
- The **compile-and-adapt loop was not run.** A two-release reth jump routinely requires op-side source adaptations (trait-method params, struct destructuring, re-export/rename churn — see `rust/UPDATING-RETH.md`). None of that is in this PR yet.

## Remaining work (before un-drafting)

1. Regenerate all three lockfiles against the new rev.
2. Run the compile-and-adapt loop to green across all three workspaces (`cargo check --workspace --tests`), then `cargo build -p op-reth`, `just fmt-fix`, `just lint`, `just test`.
3. Consider folding in #21523 (drop the replicated `SlotPreimages` now that upstream is `pub`).
4. Run the reth-update AI review (`docs/ai/reth-update-review.md`).

Draft until the above lands and CI is green.

topPRs.title: op-e2e/actions: run the action tests on the out-of-process op-reth-test-engine
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Switches `op-e2e/actions` to run against the out-of-process `op-reth-test-engine` (stacked on #21242), selected by `OP_E2E_ACTIONS_EL=reth-test-engine`. The default stays op-geth, and CI now runs the whole actions suite on **both** ELs.

## Gate: same pass-set on both ELs

Full sweep over all 13 `op-e2e/actions` packages at this head: **identical per-test results on both ELs** (225+ tests) — including the reorg suite (ReorgFlipFlop, DeepReorg, rewind, Holocene invalid-payload replacement), EL-sync (all 5 sync tests via the in-process sync-pump emulation), batcher garbage/blob paths, sequencer drift, altda challenge/expire, supernode rewind, and the engine-API tests. The only intended divergence:

- `RestartOpGeth` (op-geth persistent-DataDir restart-recovery) is geth-gated — impossible against an ephemeral subprocess. Its durable behavior is covered on **both** ELs by the new `RestartEngineFreshState`: restart the engine with all state lost; op-node resets against the wiped engine, re-derives the safe chain from L1 (safety + finality restored), and the sequencer re-builds the identical deposit-only unsafe chain. The geth-only test is deleted in the stacked deletion PR.
- One rare pre-existing-style flake was investigated and ruled out as a divergence: `FinalizeWhileSyncing` failed once in ~45+ runs, does not touch any of the new wiring (no peering/pump), and did not reproduce in 25 dedicated runs on the pre-wiring base.

## Go-side switch (mechanical rewrites, each enumerable)

- ~100 `engine.L2Chain()` sites → backend-agnostic helpers (`LatestHeader`/`SafeHeader`/`FinalizedHeader`/`BlockByNumber` over the eth RPC).
- `ActL2IncludeTx` reframed onto the engine's parking buffer (`optest_includeNextTx`); `RemainingBlockGas`/`ForcedEmpty` via `optest_*`; blob-tx rejection asserts each EL's own irreducible message.
- EL-sync p2p emulation: a package registry maps synthetic enode IDs to reth backends; `AddPeers` starts a per-peer sync pump that backfills `optest_syncTarget`-signalled gaps via `optest_blockPayloadByNumber`→`optest_importBlock`, never moving safe/finalized — reproducing op-geth's post-snap-sync state and log lines.

## Engine additions the switch forced (same crate as #21242)

- **Reorg support**: `new_payload` records every validated block; forkchoice update canonicalizes via `NewCanonicalChain::Reorg` (the engine-tree pattern), so alternate forks, flip-flops, and rewinds work. Invalid payload attributes surface as `-38003` so op-node falls back to deposits-only blocks.
- **Engine-API-faithful canonicalization**: processed payloads stay non-canonical until FCU (the geth engine test asserts exactly this gap).
- Richer reads (`eth_call`/`estimateGas`, OP-enriched receipts, historical `eth_getProof`) plus differential tests proving op-node decodes/validates reth receipts-roots and proofs, and that `eth_estimateGas` matches op-geth byte-for-byte on the action-test genesis.

## CI

`go-actions-tests-reth` runs `./op-e2e/actions/...` on the reth engine (binary from `rust-workspace-binaries`, `REQUIRE_RUST_ENGINE=1` + hard binary check so provisioning bugs fail loudly), wired into `ci-gate`. The geth side keeps running in `go-tests-short`/`go-tests-full`, so this PR puts the A/B comparison permanently in CI.

Part of #21196 (Go side) and #20415 (engine design).

topPRs.title: fix(op-challenger): advance anchors for super permissioned games
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Adds lifecycle-only handling for `SuperPermissionedDisputeGame` games so finalized games can advance their `AnchorStateRegistry` without making game type 5 playable.

Separates lifecycle support from trace playability, registers lifecycle bindings independently of configured players, routes supported games through post-game handling, and simulates `setAnchorState(game)` against the game-selected registry before submission. Adds an acceptance scenario using the real type-5 proposer and op-challenger, verifying that the ASR advances to a type-5 anchor after the finality delay.

Closes ethereum-optimism/optimism#21708

Tested with the focused SuperPermissioned acceptance scenario, affected Go package suites, and `just lint-go`.

topPRs.title: feat(kona-sp1): execute super-range range proofs
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
## Summary

`super-range` now proves optimistic per-chain transitions over timestamp spans instead of only committing claimed outputs. The range proof is rectangular over `timestamp x dependency-set chains`, binds the previous super root for every timestamp, and runs witness-backed derivation for every progressing transition.

Range execution now:
- reads one proof-wide witness blob for the whole range and reuses its preimage/blob data across all `(timestamp, chain)` transitions
- constructs each transition boot from public super-range inputs plus preimage-linked output roots and L2 headers, instead of loading per-transition witness boot inputs
- treats timestamps before the chain’s next L2 block as no-ops
- derives exactly one next block for progressing transitions
- passes the canonical interop dependency set into the derivation pipeline, preserving message-expiry overrides

Aggregation validation now has enough public data to bind range proofs to consolidation outputs: the first range timestamp must use the game starting root, later timestamps must use the previous consolidation result, and optimistic block/output commitments must match consolidation inputs.

Consolidation remains intentionally shallow in this PR: it sanity-checks that claimed consolidated outputs match the optimistic outputs and carries the claimed super root forward. Full interop message graph consolidation is still follow-up work.

## Meta

Part of https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21576
